title: ISO 19650 in Practice
subtitle: Delivering a Compliant Information Model

trainer.name: Mayanja Davis
trainer.evidence: Information Manager, Kampala Uganda Temple - a live ISO 19650-2 information management regime with BEP, MIDP and audited CDE.

pointsBasis: 1 point per contact hour - CONFIRM against the board's current scale
mode: In-person, computer lab or laptop-equipped venue. Online variant available.
audience: Registered architects, engineers, quantity surveyors and construction managers in project delivery roles
prerequisite: Working familiarity with a BIM authoring tool. No prior standards knowledge assumed.

outcomes.text: the parties, roles and information requirement chain defined in ISO 19650-1 (OIR to AIR to PIR to EIR) and state which party owes which information to whom.
a compliant information container name from a project brief, correctly populating all seven fields, and explain the function of each field.
an information container through the four CDE states and assign the correct suitability or authorization code and revision code at each transition.
the core clauses of a BIM Execution Plan, and distinguish a pre-appointment from a post-appointment BEP.
a Master Information Delivery Plan from a delivery programme, identifying deliverables, responsible parties and target dates.
an existing project's information management against the standard and name at least three specific non-conformances with their remedies.
outcomes.assessedBy: Exercise 4 (private self-audit) - deliberately not examined, as a delegate cannot be marked on a project the examiner has not seen.

runsheet.title: Opening - why information management fails
runsheet.body: Three anonymised regional case failures: a rejected donor submission, a handover with no asset data, a coordination cycle that never converged. What each one cost.

runsheet.title: Module 1 - The standard, decoded
runsheet.body: ISO 19650-1 concepts. The three parties. The information requirement chain. Level of Information Need. What -2 adds for the delivery phase, and what -5 requires on security.

runsheet.title: Module 2 - Naming and classification
runsheet.body: The container naming convention field by field, and why each exists. Classification systems, and when they are contractually required.

runsheet.title: Module 3 - The CDE and its state machine
runsheet.body: The four containers and their permissions. Suitability codes for shared information, authorization codes for published. Revision codes. The central lesson: a shared drive is not a CDE.

runsheet.title: Module 4 - The BEP and the MIDP
runsheet.body: The two documents that turn intent into obligation. Pre- versus post-appointment BEP. The MIDP as contractual spine, with the TIDP beneath it.

runsheet.title: Module 5 - Proving compliance
runsheet.body: How you demonstrate conformance when challenged: audit trail, model validation, measurable naming and tagging compliance. Automating the check versus doing it by inspection.

runsheet.title: Assessment and close
runsheet.body: Fifteen questions mapped to outcomes 1-5. Toolkit distribution.

clinic.note: Outside the accredited hours. Announced twice as optional and not required for points. This is where software is installed. Keeping the boundary clean protects the accreditation.

neutralityRules: Modules 1-4 are taught standard-first and tool-agnostic. Exercises 1-3 are done on paper and in a spreadsheet. A delegate who leaves and buys nothing must still have received full value.
Software appears only as the instructor's working method, in Module 5. Naming alternatives (ACC, Revizto, BIMcollab) strengthens the course rather than weakening it.
The commercial offer sits outside the accredited hours. The four contact hours end at 13:00; the optional clinic starts at 13:15.
